title: Last Weekend
grammarNote: This lesson covers the regular preterite (-ar/-er/-ir) plus the high-frequency irregulars fui, hice, tuve, estuve, and fue, along with past time markers (ayer, anoche, el fin de semana pasado, hace dos días) and sequencing connectors (primero, luego, después, al final). Every action described is a single, completed past event.

phrases.target: El fin de semana pasado fui a la playa
phrases.native: Last weekend I went to the beach
phrases.phonetic: el feen deh seh-MAH-nah pah-SAH-doh fwee ah lah PLAH-yah
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Fui' is the irregular preterite of ir (to go), identical in form to the preterite of ser; 'el fin de semana pasado' means 'last weekend'.

exampleSentence.target: El fin de semana pasado fui a la playa con mi familia.
exampleSentence.native: Last weekend I went to the beach with my family.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Fui' shares its form between ir and ser in the preterite — context tells you which verb is meant; here 'a la playa' signals movement, so it's from ir.
phrases.memoryHook: Fui sounds like 'phooey' — 'phooey, I already went (fui) there and I'm back'.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: Last weekend I went to the beach
practiceItems.answer: El fin de semana pasado fui a la playa

practiceItems.prompt: El fin de semana pasado ___ a la playa.
¿Adónde fuiste el fin de semana pasado?
practiceItems.answer: El fin de semana pasado fui a la playa

phrases.native: First I had breakfast with my family
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Desayuné' is the regular preterite of desayunar (-ar verb) for 'yo'; 'primero' ('first') introduces the first event in a sequence of past actions.

exampleSentence.target: Primero desayuné con mi familia y luego salimos.
exampleSentence.native: First I had breakfast with my family and then we went out.

phrases.grammarNote: Regular -ar preterite for 'yo' ends in -é: desayunar → desayuné, just like hablar → hablé or caminar → caminé.
phrases.memoryHook: Desayuné ends in -é like café — pair your morning coffee with the memory of that -é ending.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: First I had breakfast with my family
¿Qué hiciste primero el sábado por la mañana?

phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Hice' is the irregular preterite of hacer (to do/make) for 'yo'; 'luego' ('then/next') moves the story to the second event.

exampleSentence.target: Luego hice unas compras en el mercado.
exampleSentence.native: Then I did some shopping at the market.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Hacer' is irregular in the preterite: hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicieron — no accent on 'hice', unlike the regular -é endings.
phrases.memoryHook: Hice sounds like 'ee-seh' — 'easy', it was easy, I already did (hice) it.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: Then I did some shopping

phrases.target: Después comí tacos con mis amigos
phrases.native: Afterward I ate tacos with my friends
phrases.phonetic: des-PWES koh-MEE TAH-kos kon mees ah-MEE-gos
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Comí' is the regular preterite of comer (-er verb) for 'yo'; 'después' ('afterward') signals the next step in the sequence.

exampleSentence.target: Después comí tacos con mis amigos en la calle.
exampleSentence.native: Afterward I ate tacos with my friends on the street.

phrases.grammarNote: Regular -er preterite for 'yo' ends in -í: comer → comí, the same pattern -ir verbs use, like salir → salí.
phrases.memoryHook: Comí rhymes with 'so me' — 'so, me' ate all the tacos already.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: Afterward I ate tacos with my friends
practiceItems.answer: Después comí tacos con mis amigos

practiceItems.prompt: ¿Qué comiste con tus amigos ese día?
practiceItems.answer: Después comí tacos con mis amigos

phrases.native: In the end I was very tired
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Estuve' is the irregular preterite of estar for 'yo', used here for a temporary state; 'al final' ('in the end/finally') closes the sequence of events.

exampleSentence.target: Al final estuve muy cansado, pero feliz.
exampleSentence.native: In the end I was very tired, but happy.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Estar' is irregular in the preterite: estuve, estuviste, estuvo, estuvimos, estuvieron — no written accents, unlike the regular -í/-é endings.
phrases.memoryHook: Estuve sounds like 'es-TOO-vay' — 'it was too much', so I ended up exhausted.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: In the end I was very tired
¿Cómo te sentiste al final del fin de semana?

dialogue.scenario: On Monday morning, a friend asks what you did over the weekend.

turns.speaker: npc
turns.line: ¡Hola! ¿Qué hiciste el fin de semana pasado?
turns.native: Hi! What did you do last weekend?

turns.speaker: npc

turns.native: That's great! And what did you do first when you got there?

turns.speaker: npc

turns.speaker: learner
hints: Después comí tacos con mis amigos

turns.speaker: npc

turns.speaker: npc
